definitions.branch_target_shape: empty | hex (0x...) | dec (digits) | register (an ARM64 register name) | other, applied to the instruction target field
definitions.callee_rendering: an occurrence of '<callee>(' for the three emitted callee spellings sub_<hex>, fn_0x<hex> and sel<N>; lost is the per-file, per-callee positive difference reference minus candidate
definitions.candidate_marker: the pseudocode-callee-removals.tsv column: whole-file presence of '// trap:' and of '// indirect branch through <reg>: target not recovered' in the candidate pseudocode file, as both / indirect_branch_only / trap_only / none. It is a file property, not the removal class, and is recorded on every row.
definitions.differing_field_paths: number of ir documents whose difference set includes the field path, after removing the two added top-level objects; '.[] (length)' means the two lists had different lengths
definitions.exclusive_instruction_reason: for an address present on only one side, the nearest earlier instruction in address order that is not itself exclusive to that side; 'after_trap:<mnemonic>' when that instruction is brk/hlt/udf, otherwise 'after_<op>'
definitions.instruction_alignment: instructions are matched between the two sides by virtual address within the same function
definitions.ir_reference_only_instructions: the pseudocode-callee-removals.tsv column: instruction addresses present in that function's reference ir/*.json and absent from its candidate ir/*.json, recorded on every row of the table
definitions.lost_edge: an address-level control-flow edge the reference had and the candidate does not, over sequential adjacency inside a block plus one edge from a block's last instruction address to each successor block's start address; the effect that removed it is the candidate op at the edge's tail address
definitions.lost_edge_effects: the pseudocode-callee-removals.tsv column, an effect-occurrence count and not a count of distinct control-flow edges: its keys are keyed on the tuples in lost_edge_effects_algorithm, so one lost edge bounding a region that holds three vanished callees is counted three times. Distinct address-level lost edges are counted separately in callee-removals-aggregate.json distinct_lost_edges.
lost_edge_effects_algorithm: The entry block is the candidate block whose start_va equals the function's entry_va, and a candidate block is unreachable when no directed path of successor edges reaches it from that entry block.
The region of a candidate block is its weakly connected component in the subgraph induced by the unreachable blocks, taking a successor edge between two unreachable blocks as undirected.

A lost reference edge bounds that region when its head address falls inside the component: the head resolves to the candidate block that starts at that address, or failing that to the candidate block holding an instruction at it.
lost_edge_after_<op> is one occurrence per (file, wholly vanished callee, candidate block holding a Call to that callee, distinct candidate tail op among the lost edges bounding that block's region).
disposition_<D> is one occurrence per (file, wholly vanished callee, unreachable candidate block holding a Call to that callee).
dispatch_selector_rendering is one occurrence per (file, wholly vanished sel<N> callee), not one per lost rendering.
definitions.op_transitions: for an address present on both sides, '<reference op>-><candidate op>' when the op differs
definitions.operand_naming_direction: difflib.unified_diff(n=0) as in removed_and_added_lines; hunks that replace exactly one line with exactly one line, compared by the number of regN tokens on each side
definitions.operand_naming_fewer_register_classes: the four-way split of the fewer_registers rows is committed human adjudication of the two rendered lines, carried per row in the operand-direction-losses.tsv adjudication_class column; it is not a syntax metric inferred from the rows, so verify recounts the column against the recorded totals rather than re-deriving the class
definitions.pseudocode_line_tags: regex tags per added or removed line of a difflib.unified_diff(n=0) diff, as in removed_and_added_lines; a line can carry several tags
definitions.removed_and_added_lines: counted from difflib.unified_diff(reference_lines, candidate_lines, n=0) in Python 3, over splitlines(True) of the two files, skipping the ---/+++/@@ lines: every remaining line starting with '-' is a removed line and every one starting with '+' is an added line. The implementation matters: GNU diff -U0 and git diff -U0 group hunks differently and do not reproduce these totals.
definitions.removed_pseudocode_class: one class per differing file: no_callee_rendering_lost, fewer_renderings_same_callees, dispatch_selector_rendering_only, or vanished_behind_<ops>, where ops is the set of tail ops in that file's lost_edge_after_<op> keys, each op spelled in snake_case, in ascending op order, joined by _and_; a file can hold several unreachable regions and the ops need not all bound the same one
definitions.wholly_vanished_callee: a callee the reference rendered at least once in a file and the candidate renders nowhere in that file
